basic_details.job_title: RFRI Recruitment 2026 – Walkin for 2 Junior Project Fellow, Project Assistant Posts
basic_details.short_information: ICFRE-Rain Forest Research Institute (RFRI), Jorhat, under the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education, Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change, will hold a walk-in interview on 26 November 2026 from 9.30 am onwards at the Institute in Jorhat. Candidates are to report between 9.30 am and 10.30 am. The interview is to engage one Junior Project Fellow (JPF) at Rs. 24,000/- + HRA as admissible and one Project Assistant (PA) at Rs. 22,000/- (Fixed) per month on an externally aided project.

age_limit.details: Junior Project Fellow (JPF): upper age limit 28 years as on 01.07.2026. Project Assistant (PA): upper age limit 25 years as on 01.07.2026. Relaxation for both posts: up to 5 years for SC/ST/Women and 3 years for OBC candidates.

content_sections.heading: About RFRI
content_sections.text: ICFRE-Rain Forest Research Institute is part of the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education, under the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change, Government of India. Its letterhead gives the address as Deovan, Sotai, Jorhat-785010 (Assam). The posts are for the GoI-UNDP-GEF7 Biodiversity Project "Strengthening Institutional Capacities for Securing Biodiversity Conservation Commitments", with Dr. Dhruba J. Das, Scientist-F, as Principal Investigator and the National Biodiversity Authority, Chennai, as funding agency.

content_sections.heading: Posts and Eligibility
content_sections.text: For the JPF post, candidates having working experience in Garo Hills, Meghalaya and GIS will be preferred (desirable). Junior Project Fellow (JPF): upper age limit 28 years as on 01.07.2026. Project Assistant (PA): upper age limit 25 years as on 01.07.2026. Relaxation for both posts: up to 5 years for SC/ST/Women and 3 years for OBC candidates. The posts are purely contractual. The project is initially for 1 year. Recruitment is temporary and co-terminus with the project, and does not guarantee subsequent employment in any Institute under the Council. Candidates should check the official notification for any further eligibility detail for each post.

rows.qualification: Essential: First class Master degree in Forestry/Botany/Agriculture (Extension)/Geography
Essential: First class Bachelor Degree in Forestry/Botany/Agriculture/Geography

content_sections.heading: What to Bring
content_sections.text: Duly filled application form in the prescribed format (the form is on page 2 of the notice). Attested copies of educational qualifications from HSLC onwards, experience certificates and other relevant documents. Age proof certificate, and caste proof certificate for SC/ST/OBC candidates. One passport size photograph (the form also has space for a self-attested passport size photograph). Original certificates for verification at the time of reporting. A No Objection Certificate from the employer, for candidates working in Government/public sector undertakings or autonomous organisations.

content_sections.heading: What Happens on the Day
content_sections.text: Candidates report between 9.30 am and 10.30 am on 26 November 2026 and submit the filled application form with attested copies of their documents. Original certificates are verified at reporting. The interview is held from 9.30 am onwards. The application form also asks for the project(s) preferred, language and computer proficiency, previous work experience and any contractual obligation to serve another Government, public sector or autonomous body.

content_sections.heading: Important Instructions
content_sections.text: No TA/DA will be paid for attending the interview. Canvassing in any form will lead to disqualification of the candidate. The declaration on the form states that if any material information is found concealed or distorted, the appointment is liable to termination without notice at any point during the project. Applicants should ensure that they satisfy the eligibility criteria.

faq.question: Q1. When is the RFRI Jorhat walk-in interview?
faq.answer: The walk-in interview is on 26 November 2026 from 9.30 am onwards at ICFRE-Rain Forest Research Institute, Jorhat.

faq.question: Q2. What is the reporting time?
faq.answer: Candidates must report between 9.30 am and 10.30 am on the day of the interview, with the application form and documents.

faq.question: Q3. How many vacancies are there?
faq.answer: There are 2 posts: 1 Junior Project Fellow (JPF) and 1 Project Assistant (PA).

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification for JPF and PA?
faq.answer: JPF needs a First class Master degree in Forestry/Botany/Agriculture (Extension)/Geography. PA needs a First class Bachelor Degree in Forestry/Botany/Agriculture/Geography.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit?
faq.answer: The upper age limit is 28 years for JPF and 25 years for PA, as on 01.07.2026. Relaxation is up to 5 years for SC/ST/Women and 3 years for OBC candidates.

faq.question: Q6. What is the salary?
faq.answer: JPF gets Rs. 24,000/- + HRA as admissible per month. PA gets Rs. 22,000/- (Fixed) per month.

faq.question: Q7. Is HRA paid on top of the pay?
faq.answer: For JPF, the pay is Rs. 24,000/- + HRA as admissible. The PA pay of Rs. 22,000/- is printed as Fixed.

faq.question: Q8. Is this a permanent job?
faq.answer: No. The posts are purely contractual, temporary and co-terminus with the project, which is initially for 1 year, and do not guarantee later employment in any Institute under the Council.

faq.question: Q9. What documents should I bring?
faq.answer: Bring the filled application form, attested copies of certificates, experience certificates, age and caste proof where applicable, one passport size photograph and original certificates. Employees of Government/public sector/autonomous bodies must bring a No Objection Certificate.

faq.question: Q10. Will TA/DA be paid for the interview?
faq.answer: No. The notice states that no TA/DA will be paid for attending the interview.
